brief: Meta launched Muse on September 8, 2026, and Instinct is separately gaining adoption. Fear that turnkey AI agents let non-developer users book travel, rides, and shopping on their behalf has pressured marketplace stocks, and Wolfe ties a resulting selloff in EXPE (-5.4%), BKNG (-9.0%), DASH (-3.5%), SHOP (-8.9%), and UBER (-5.2%) to that fear. Wolfe estimates Muse could add $30-50B in medium/long-term revenue for Meta: $30B via subscriptions (5% of Meta's 3 billion users at $20/month) plus a mid-to-high single-digit billion take-rate model. Meta's edge is data, distribution, and first-mover status, since OpenAI and Google have not shipped competing consumer agents, though Wolfe expects both, plus Anthropic, to release similar agents. Wolfe's central call is that the market's disruption fear is overdone and the actual risk is MODEST, because incumbents retain moats through full-service value chains, proprietary data, their own in-app agents, and subscription programs (Uber One, DashPass) that reduce the incentive to share economics on non-incremental orders. Wolfe ranks perceived risk as Travel most exposed, then Ride Sharing, then eCommerce, then Food Delivery.
